item.text: I’ll use the supplied Deep Research Council and Platform Migration instructions to ground the memo in the packet and keep it within 250 words.

Pilot an online console on managed Chrome and Safari for dispatchers to view schedules, assign jobs and review synced inspections. Defer a packaged macOS client until dispatchers identify a native requirement. Keep technicians on managed Android 11+ for inspections, photos and up to 48 hours offline, with Room queuing submissions and WorkManager retrying them. [MIG-AW-OPS §1, MIG-AW-APP §§1–2, MIG-AW-BRIEF §1]

**Reject copying Room.** Its encryption keys are device-bound, export and restore are undocumented, and the queue holds unsent work. Preserve that queue on Android and use the server API for accepted records. The 11-screen scope and six-week estimate are unverified. [MIG-AW-APP §2, MIG-AW-API §2, MIG-AW-BRIEF §1]

**Proof of concept.** Test one staging job in both managed browsers. Verify sign-in, session renewal and CORS preflight for `PATCH` with `If-Match`. Force a stale assignment edit, require `409 Conflict`, then refresh and retry. Submit one queued Android inspection twice with the same `submissionId` and require exactly one accepted record. Let its 20-minute signed photo URL expire, renew it and retain the image until upload acknowledgement. Verify the final assignment, inspection and photo in both browsers. Browser versions, Safari compatibility and browser upload renewal remain unverified. [MIG-AW-API §§1–3, MIG-AW-OPS §2]

**Rollout gate.** Pilot with one dispatcher after both browsers pass. Measure task completion time. Expand only when assignments and inspections reconcile without loss or duplication. On failure, disable console writes, resume existing dispatch and reconcile accepted changes. [MIG-AW-OPS §2, MIG-AW-API §§1–2]
